tasks.task: Map the panels and write the layout spec

items.when: When you have the printer's dieline, the product facts and approved copy and need a panel-by-panel spec
When a back panel carries a lot of text and needs a grid, a short type list and white space
Before you settle the front, to get three hand-made alternatives to the template look
When a panel is drafted, to see where the eye lands first, what to move and what to cut
When small type is set, to check size, spacing and line length at the distance it is read

tasks.task: Write front and back pack copy panel by panel

items.when: When each panel has a fixed space and the front must win a three-second glance
When the front line is flat, to get five short lines that each take a different angle
When a line sounds like any product, to make it short, true and easy to picture
When the copy will not fit the panel and must lose words without losing the point
When a line is witty, to test a shopper gets what the product is before the joke
When the front names features and not the one benefit a shopper would pick it up for

tasks.task: Explore front panel directions

items.when: Before any layout, to find the one idea, one feeling and one symbol the front should carry
When the pack look is undecided, to compare three mood board directions and merge a pick
When a direction needs a picture, to try one pack idea as four different treatments
When there are several fronts, to compare them beside the packs they will sit next to
When a front is drafted, to test what a shopper takes in at a glance and at thumbnail size
When a redesign risks being so new that current buyers no longer spot the product

tasks.task: List the details the label must carry

items.when: When you need the list of required details for the product type and each market it sells in
When the label makes claims, to sort each as fine, needs proof or cut, with safer wording
When the details are set, to catch typos and one name spelt two ways across panels

tasks.task: Test the front panel on shelf and as a thumbnail

items.when: Before print, to review the front against the competitors beside it on a shelf or search page
When you want a second scored test of what reads at a glance and at small size
When the pack must match the site, emails and ads, to score what each one says
When the front is clear but carries no cue that buyers would know the brand by

tasks.task: Write the packaging brief

items.when: When a new product or pack format has a launch date and needs steps from brief to proof
When a designer needs one brief covering materials, format, panels and unboxing
When the client sets no limits, to fix firm rules for the pack before any layout
When assets are scattered, to plan a one-page visual sheet and list what is missing
When the brief keeps adding messages and the pack needs less on it

tasks.task: Request the dieline and spec from the printer

items.when: At the start of the job, to get the dieline, artwork guide and proof dates before any layout
When the pack has not been quoted yet, to write the request in the maker's terms
When printers have quoted, to compare price, minimum order, lead time and risk

tasks.task: Preflight artwork and check the printer's proof

items.when: Before the file is sent and again when the proof comes back, to check it line by line
When the legal panel uses very small type, to check it can still be read
When text sits on a coloured or printed background, to check each pair is readable
When a printed sample arrives, to pass or fail it line by line against the spec
When samples go back and forth, to track fixes and stop at three rounds

tasks.task: Build a layout system across a product range

items.when: When several flavours, scents or sizes look messy side by side, or before adding variants
Before the system, to list every product type and variant the range must hold
When each variant needs its own colour, to plan a small palette with one job per colour
When the range needs firm rules for what stays fixed and what changes per variant
When variant colours are picked, to check the text reads on every one

tasks.task: Write a copy system for a product range

items.when: When every variant needs the same panel structure with its own name and lines
When variants need names, to get a family of names from one root to choose from
When the range has no written voice, to set tone and word lists before the lines
When the lines are drafted, to find where a variant drifts from the brand's voice

tasks.task: Spec a label or sticker layout

items.when: When a jar label, bottle wrap or sticker needs zones, sizes and safe areas written out
When the maker has no brand fonts, to compare three pairs with sizes
When the label is small and crowded and needs a strict grid
When the label is drafted, to check the smallest text at arm's length

tasks.task: Plan the unboxing and insert cards

items.when: When the product ships in a box or mailer and you plan what the buyer sees, in order
When the unboxing feels plain, to get matched sight, touch and sound cues with costs
When the insert, note and gift must be costed against order value and margin
When the client wants one guided run to an unboxing plan built on their order data
When an insert card is drafted, to check what the eye lands on first

tasks.task: Check on-pack claims against proof

items.when: When a claim such as organic or vegan has its own label rules in a market
When the pack makes claims, to match each one to the evidence the maker holds
When the front rests on one claim, to test it is real, unique and strong
When a claim fails, to get safer wording that still sells

tasks.task: List pack components for recycling labels and EPR data

items.when: When choosing a recycling label, when materials change, or when a producer needs data by component
When the pack has many parts, to list each part with its maker and cost

tasks.task: Handle a label change and reprint

items.when: When a recipe, supplier, size, address or material changes, or a new market is added
When the change may alter what the label has to carry
When the same fact also appears in ads, pages and emails and all must change together
Before the reprint, to check the changed panels word by word

tasks.task: Run a new pack from brief to approved proof

items.when: When a maker moves from home-printed labels to printed packs with a shop date
When the launch date is fixed, to date every step from samples to warehouse with owners
When someone else will fill and pack the product and their limits shape the pack
When the plan has no slack, to correct the dates by how such jobs really go

tasks.task: Make pack mockup images to show the client

items.when: Before any image, to write the pack's true details and the lines that lock them
When a direction needs a picture and you want a prompt, the exact size and a file plan
When a flat design must be placed on a pack shape or cut out cleanly
When a mockup comes back, to check the label text and shape were not changed
When you need a vector draft of a label or icon that can be scaled
When a photo the client owns must be extended or cleaned up for the mockup

tasks.task: Compare packaging quotes and cost per unit

items.when: When quotes use different units, currencies or delivery terms and must be put on one basis
When you have two or more quotes pasted, to get one table and the cash each needs
When the pack price is known, to see what it does to cost per unit sold

tasks.task: Adapt a pack for another country or language

items.when: When the pack enters a new market and the required details differ
When images and copy need local language, sizes and required labels for each country
When panel text must be translated in a natural tone with consistent terms

tasks.task: Write the brand story for the back panel

items.when: When the story must fit a fixed back-panel space beside the required details
When the founder has a long true story, to map it and cut it to what moves a reader
When the maker has only rough notes on how they started
When the story is over the space, to cut it without losing the point

tasks.task: Plan a gift set or seasonal sleeve

items.when: When a sleeve or gift box needs its own panel map on top of the standard pack
When the season needs an idea, to compare gift, bundle and pre-order options
When the set must hold margin, to fix what goes in it before any design

tasks.task: Review a current pack and rank the fixes

items.when: When a pack is on sale and the maker asks why it is missed on shelf or in search
When reviews exist, to find what buyers say about the pack, the label and opening it
When the pack sits beside the site and ads, to score what each one says
When every panel is full and the fix is to take things away

always.when: Before any pack work for a brand with a live site: colours, fonts and voice
When the pack states a number, award or claim you cannot trace to the maker

helpers.when: When the brand has no logo, palette or type to build the pack from
When label rules for a regulated product or market need a proper check
When the pack format, material or supplier is still open
When the finished pack needs real photos for listings and ads
When panels must be translated for another market
When the launch needs ads and page copy to match the pack

gaps: No library item writes on-pack copy panel by panel to a fixed space; only the kit skill does
No library item turns a dieline into a panel map and layout spec
No library item lists required label details by product type and market: allergens, nutrition, ingredients and date marks
No library item covers recycling labels, EPR data or choosing lower-waste materials
No library item covers barcodes: number source, size, quiet zone and placement
No library item preflights packaging artwork or checks a printer's proof for bleed, spot colours and minimum type
No library item chooses a pack format or plans a shipping box and its protection
No library item builds a layout or colour-coding system across a range of variants
No library item covers retailer and Amazon packaging rules such as shelf-ready packs and warehouse labels
No library item makes a mockup from a dieline, and no tool guide covers Illustrator or pack mockup tools
